The cited value of 0.1 h⁻¹ and the configured value of 0.1 min⁻¹ differ by a factor of 60; the comparison alone does not demonstrate a software unit error. All three no-CAR controls and six seed 0 control-normalized comparisons are complete, including spatial zero-effector invariants. These are single-seed conditional background trajectories, not measured or three-seed calibrated growth distributions. The nine fixed growth/background challenges have completed native validation and scientific review. All six prescribed growth alternatives are technically accepted and substantively reviewed. Each has higher living-target counts than the baseline three-seed envelope at all 96 positive saved hours. Their interval-average increases over the paired baseline are 32.8594, 80.9479 and 118.9792 for growth A, and 86.9323, 152.8906 and 192.3333 for growth B in 2D, 3D and local entry. The corresponding endpoints are 73/169/368 and 75/294/518. This establishes material dependence of these configured outputs on the assigned growth scale. The source quantities are net population growth fits in distinct systems, while the active model uses oxygen/pressure-modified single-cell cycle entry and cytokine effects. No compatible untreated growth/pressure/cytokine observation model or measured mapping is supplied by these checks.

The five-case, 485-frame IL2 effector-local exposure audit is complete. Loss of 0.01 min⁻¹ and zero yield 1.948 and 12.041 times baseline-seed 0 AUC of the current living-population mean. That is not tracked-cell dose or mean nonlinear response. The IL2-to-cycle K/Hill/cap and CD4/CD8 equality remain conditional; growth/background checks are complete and substantively reviewed. The cited source concerns a different observable. It neither validates the present constants nor justifies replacing n=2 with n=1. Molecular concentration scaling and the mapping to cycle entry remain absent. The three background-loss alternatives retain all effector division parameters. Endpoint effector counts increase by 359, 397 and 371 in 2D, 3D and local entry, while target interval means change by -4.8490, +5.1823 and +3.0938. The altered population balance materially affects effector counts without a uniformly signed target change. Changing death alone does not identify the IL2-to-cycle scale, response Hill law, cap or CD4/CD8 equality. The current living-population exposure audit remains distinct from tracked-cell dose and a calibrated division response.

No-CAR controls and their zero-immune invariants are complete. They constrain net conditional trajectories, not individual apoptosis/necrosis hazards. Executed oxygen-modified rates remain distinct from XML constants; the nine kinetic challenges are complete; the quantitative background-loss basis remains unresolved. All three background-loss alternatives are technically accepted and substantively reviewed. They change the reference equality of unstimulated effector division and apoptosis as prescribed. Local-entry field changes are material even when target count changes are below the reporting tolerance. A bound fitted in another short population assay does not calibrate the active apoptosis hazard, target apoptosis/necrosis, or executed oxygen-dependent rates. The challenge does not identify separate growth and death hazards.
